summary: Answering the question put to this round: yes, one. aBrokenReaderViewIsREPORTED's javadoc claims it constrains the sweep's PLUMBING; MEASURED, the plumbing mutation it names still survives, and the test is fully subsumed by five pre-existing ReaderInvariantsTest cases. Every other assertion added this round was mutation-verified live: the ackEvents floor, the ackFloorAlwaysZero flag, and AckOrderTest's epoch/sequence role assertion.

findings.title: R4-2 is NOT closed and the javadoc says it is: dropping the sweep's `violations.addAll` around `checkReader` still leaves the whole :sequencer suite GREEN -- MEASURED
findings.failure_scenario: The javadoc says 'review measured that dropping the addAll while keeping the call leaves it green, so the count does not pin that the verdict is CONSUMED. This hands the same checker the same shape of view the loop builds ... constraining checker, wiring and plumbing together rather than the loop counter alone.' The last clause is false. I applied exactly the mutation the comment names, in a review tree over the staged bytes: CommitProtocolSimulation.java:351-352, `violations.addAll(ReaderInvariants.checkReader(backing, PREFIX, ReaderInvariants.ReaderView.of(reader)));` -> `ReaderInvariants.checkReader(backing, PREFIX, ReaderInvariants.ReaderView.of(reader));`. Verified in bytecode (`invokestatic ReaderInvariants.checkReader` immediately followed by `pop`), then `./gradlew :sequencer:test -Dsweep.seeds=60` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Both new tests pass. The reason is structural, not calibration: aBrokenReaderViewIsREPORTED builds its OWN MemoryBinStore, its OWN `new ReaderView(committed, Map.of())`, and calls `ReaderInvariants.checkReader` directly. It shares no line with the sweep loop, so it cannot observe whether the sweep loop keeps or discards the verdict. `readersChecked` still counts iterations, which is the finding verbatim. Concrete consequence: someone optimising `checkReader` out of the O(E-squared) loop against the 60s budget -- the exact person the neighbouring comment at :208-212 names -- discards I3 and I4's drop clause across all 1,000 seeds, the sweep prints '74,170 readers judged' and passes, and backlog-done.md's landed row plus backlog-notes.md's 'checkReader carries I3 and I4's DROP clause' both keep asserting that half of M4's completion condition is checked. Second, weaker problem with the same test: it constrains nothing new. Disabling the I4 drop arm (`else if (applied < want.getValue())` -> `else if (false)`) reddens aBrokenReaderViewIsREPORTED AND five pre-existing tests -- ReaderInvariantsTest.aReaderThatDROPPEDACommittedRecordVIOLATESI4, aReaderThatSAWNoStreamsAtAllVIOLATESI4, aSTALEViewIsReportedAsI4AndTheCONTRACTSaysSo, TWOStreamsBrokenInOPPOSITEDirectionsAreBOTHReported, ReaderInvariantsScopeTest.anEpochSEALEDBeforeItsCONTINUEIsNOWJudgedAgainstItsInheritedBase. So it is a duplicate of coverage that already existed, wearing a javadoc that claims a seam it does not have. Two ways out, and the cheap one is honest prose: either delete the test and correct the javadoc to say the plumbing is NOT pinned and file it as a row, or make the sweep assert on something only the addAll can produce -- e.g. have the seed-0 fixture in aBrokenReaderViewIsREPORTED go through CommitProtocolSimulation.run with a deliberately stale/broken reader view injected into the loop, so `run.violations()` must carry the I4.

verified_from_previous_rounds: M4.13-R4-1 (ack trace emission claimed but absent) is FIXED and the fix is live. MEASURED at 60 seeds: removing the two leader emissions at CommitProtocolSimulation.java:317-318 reddens theInvariantsHoldAcrossEverySeed on the `ackEvents >= SEEDS * 5` floor; removing only the slot-0 CONTINUE at :213 reddens it on ackFloorAlwaysZero (CommitProtocolSweepTest.java:222). The floor is absolute, not relative, so an empty trace no longer satisfies it. Also checked it does not misfire while bisecting: -Dsweep.seeds=1, 2 and 5 all pass.

R4-3 (readersChecked floor cited no measurement) is fixed and the number checks out: my own 60-seed run printed 'sweep: 60 seeds in 1123 ms, 4576 readers judged' = 76.3/seed against the comment's 74.17 and a floor of 10.
R4-4 (unbounded duplicated failure report) is fixed: one line per seed plus '(+N more on this seed)'.
The -Dsweep.seeds forwarding in binjava.java-conventions.gradle.kts works -- MEASURED, the run above reported 60 seeds, not 1000.

AckOrderTest.java:198-221 is a genuine new constraint, not prose. MEASURED: swapping the terms in AckOrderInvariants' own-write arm (AckOrderInvariants.java:118-119, `e.epoch()`/`e.sequence()` transposed) now reddens ONECHAINSConfirmationsDoNotSatisfyANOTHERS. The `acked(2, 2)` -> `acked(2, 5)` change is what makes the roles observable, and the assertion is on the full 'epoch 2 acked sequence 5' substring rather than 'epoch 2'. This closes what backlog-notes.md deferred to this row.

Cost lens: nothing in this diff adds an object-store request on any production path. The only new store traffic is test scaffolding on MemoryBinStore, and it scales with EPOCHS (failovers), not with records, shards, partitions or indices. The O(E-squared) growth is already owned by M4.24 and M4.13h.
